title: Hulu Renews The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County for 20 Episodes
excerpt:
The reality spinoff has secured a second season after a strong debut.
Its first season generated 35 million viewing hours worldwide in 11 days.
body_md:
Hulu has renewed The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County for a second season consisting of 20 episodes. The substantial order follows the launch of the reality spinoff's eight-episode first season and reflects strong viewing results across Hulu and Disney+.

The debut season premiered on November 12, 2026, and generated 35 million hours of viewing worldwide during its first 11 days. Its premiere performed 12 percent ahead of the fifth-season premiere of the original series. Across the wider franchise, global viewing has exceeded half a billion hours. These figures measure hours watched, not the number of unique viewers.

The spinoff follows a group of young mothers and social-media personalities in Orange County, California. While the original The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives is set in Utah, this edition explores relationships and social dynamics in a different environment. The first-season cast included Ashleigh Pease, Aspyn Ovard, Jen Affleck, Bobbi Althoff, Avery Woods, Salomé Andrea, McCall DaPron, Jordan McClanahan and Madison Bontempo.

There are direct links between the two shows. Mayci Neeley, who appears in the original series and is McCall DaPron's sister, made a cameo during the spinoff's first season. Jen Affleck is also associated with both programs. The women do not all share the same religious identity or level of involvement with the Mormon church, and those differences contribute to the show's interpersonal tensions.

Before the first season premiered, Aspyn Ovard explained that although she had been baptized into the Mormon church, she no longer identified as Mormon. She nevertheless acknowledged the influence of Mormon culture on her upbringing, marriage and early motherhood. She also suggested that women with different religious and social outlooks could learn from one another, an idea that reflects the program's wider focus on identity and community.

The series is produced by Jeff Jenkins Productions alongside 3BMG and Walt Disney Television Alternative. A 20-episode second season has been confirmed, but the announcement does not specify its premiere date or guarantee the return of every first-season cast member. Those details remain to be announced.
